title: Adaptive pinning strategy and compatibility notes for new open-model intake
creator: Rohan Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a concrete, implementation-friendly set of requirements for onboarding new open models into the Redwood model catalog that balances safety, compatibility, and user control. This ticket defines an adaptive version-pinning strategy, compatibility annotation requirements, and acceptance criteria for the intake flow so engineering and DX teams can implement catalog ingestion, UI prompts, and runtime fallback behavior.

Background and motivation:
- Recent onboarding PRDs have left ambiguity around whether to require strict model-version pinning vs. allowing open 'latest' aliases for open-source variants. Product teams want predictable behavior for Dedicated/Private customers while enabling flexibility for Hosted users.
- Engineering requests explicit compatibility metadata so runtime can select kernel/quantization profiles automatically.
- Legal/security flagged potential export/compliance concerns around some community models; intake should surface this.

Problem statement:
- Lack of clear pinning defaults causes unexpected model regressions in production when upstream commits change weights or tokenizer behaviors.
- Missing compatibility notes lead to manual tuning and rollout friction for runtime.
- Intake form and PRD needs acceptance criteria to unblock ENG work and security review.

Scope (In-scope):
- Define default pinning policy for three catalog tiers: verified, community, experimental.
- Required compatibility fields for each intake (architecture, tokenizer family, sequence-length limits, recommended quantization profile, known incompatibilities).
- UI copy and UX flow changes for model owners to supply pin preferences and compatibility notes.
- Runtime fallback behavior spec when requested pinned version is unavailable.
- Security checklist items required before model is promoted to 'verified'.

Scope (Out-of-scope):
- Automated kernel selection implementation (ENG-7012 will own execution).
- Full audit logging backend changes for Private customers (separate infra ticket).

Requirements (functional):
- Intake form must require a "compatibility metadata" block with these string fields: architecture, tokenizer, supported_max_sequence, recommended_quant_profile, known_issues_link (URL).
- For "verified" models, intake must require a strict semantic version or commit SHA pin (user-provided) and a file artifact URL (checksum).
- For "community" models, default pinning is to a "major.minor" semantic pin with option to pin to exact commit; UI must warn about "rolling" tags.
- For "experimental" models, default is rolling/latest but UI must show an explicit "risk acknowledgement" checkbox.
- Console must show a concise compatibility summary on the model card and expose a machine-readable compatibility blob via the catalog API (catalog/v1/models/<id>/compatibility).
- Runtime fallback policy: on pinned-version failure, attempt (in order) local cache -> pinned-compatible variant -> configured fallback model; all attempts must be logged and surfaced to the Console Rollouts page.
- Acceptance: Security review must be completed for verified and community models before enabling for Dedicated/Private tenants.

Acceptance criteria (clear pass/fail):
1) Intake UX accepts and stores the full compatibility block and displays it on the model card. (QA: create a test model and verify all fields render and are searchable)
2) Console warns users when selecting rolling/latest for community/experimental tiers with a dismissible acknowledgement. (QA: simulate onboarding with rolling tag and confirm ack required)
3) API exposes compatibility blob as JSON string at the documented endpoint and returns 200 for created models. (QA: post a model; GET compatibility endpoint)
4) Pinning rules enforced for each tier: verified -> strict pin + checksum, community -> major.minor default, experimental -> rolling by default. (QA: attempt to publish violating rules and confirm validation errors)
5) Runtime fallback flow documented and demoed with ENG using a synthetic failure scenario; logs and Console Rollouts show the attempted fallbacks. (QA: run simulated failure and capture logs)
6) Security checklist run and recorded for at least two sample community models and one verified model. (QA: Security sign-off attached in model metadata)

UX notes and copy guidance:
- Add inline help text for each compatibility field to reduce ambiguity (examples included in PRD link).
- Model card should show an icon for "Pinned" with hover tooltip that explains the pin level and last-pinned timestamp.
- Warning modal copy for rolling tags must include recommended mitigations (pin to SHA for Dedicated customers).

API and Console implications:
- New catalog API endpoint (compatibility blob) — engineering to define schema with product and runtime owners. The product side requires the field be stored as plain JSON string in the catalog document.
- Console must surface pin metadata and last-verified timestamp.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (catalog UI + API): validate ingestion and display for new models only.
- Phase 2 (bulk migration): offer "retrofit compatibility" workflow for existing community models with a soft deadline and email nudges.
- Phase 3 (runtime enforcement): runtime validation enforced for verified/community during rollout window.

Open questions (action items):
- Q1: For community tier, do we allow "weekly" rolling channels as a middle-ground? Action: Product decision needed by 2025-03-11.
- Q2: Should we accept tokenizer mapping heuristics (automatically infer tokenizer family) or require explicit input? Action: Ask Research/Applied ML to prototype inference by 2025-03-07.
- Q3: What is the exact catalog API field name/shape? Action: ENG & PM sync (ENG-6123) on 2025-03-05.

Progress updates and review history:
- 2025-02-20: Initial draft PRD created by Rohan.
- 2025-02-25: Engineering triage meeting; ENG requested concrete acceptance criteria for runtime fallback (added above).
- 2025-02-27: Security raised export control checklist requirement; added to in-scope.
- 2025-03-02: Design reviewed UX copy and provided mockups (link below). Minor copy changes incorporated.
- 2025-03-04: First engineering review completed; ENG requested API endpoint name confirmation and example payload.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Users may misconfigure and pin incorrect tokenizers leading to silent failures. Mitigation: add validation and tokenizer compatibility checks in PRD and plan a soft launch with telemetry.
- Risk: Security review delay blocking Verified promotion. Mitigation: parallelize security checklist run with intake review and add gating flags in Console.

Next steps (owners and dates):
- Product: finalize decision on weekly channel by 2025-03-11 (owner: Rohan).
- ENG: finalize API field shape and provide example payload by 2025-03-05 (owner: Maria Santos).
- Design: handoff final mocks and copy by 2025-03-06 (owner: Anika Bose).
- Security: complete export control checklist template by 2025-03-10 (owner: Jordan Blake).

Notes for reviewers:
Please focus review on the acceptance criteria and the fallbacks ordering. If you disagree with the pinning defaults, propose concrete alternatives and list trade-offs.
